text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: GPU capacity exhaustion affecting inference queue - high error rate on /v1/generate. Escalation to on-call infra (maria).

maria: seeing big queue backlog on the GPU pool, autoscaler isn't provisioning new nodes. metrics: gpu-queue-length = ~2400, 90th latency = 3.2s -> 18s for queued jobs. customers hitting 503/429 spikes.

kevin: confirmed - cluster-autoscaler logs show repeated failures when launching nodegroup: 
```
I0109 09:11:15 main.go:123] Failed to scale up: error running ASG API: AccessDenied: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/infra-autoscaler-role is not authorized to perform: autoscaling:CreateAutoScalingGroup on resource: arn:aws:autoscaling:us-west-2:123456789012:autoScalingGroup:*:autoScalingGroupName/*
```

maria: that looks like an IAM permission change. but also saw recent launch template update rolled out yesterday - could be incompatible with k8s taint/labels.

sahil: adding logs from cluster-autoscaler: 
```
W0109 09:12:02 scale_up.go:410] max node group size reached for node group 'gpu-pool-prod' (max: 12 current: 12)
I0109 09:12:02 scale_up.go:435] No more resources to schedule pods, but node group is at max size
```

jen: so two things: (1) ASG/max size is saturated, (2) IAM errors when autoscaler tries different nodegroups. which one is currently blocking additional capacity?

maria: ASG max reached first. customer load spiked and consumed all 12 nodes. Attempts to create a new nodegroup trigged IAM AccessDenied. also some launched nodes failed to join due to a taint on gpu nodes not matching kubelet label, so pods stayed pending.

ops-bot: automatic mitigation suggestion: 1) increase ASG max temporarily 2) fallback CPU queue routing 3) manual nodegroup create with known-good launch template

alex: I'm going to manually open a short-term capacity window: requesting increase of gpu-pool-prod max to 18. who can apply?

kevin: I can patch ASG, but we need approval for safety window. jen, can you greenlight temporary bump for 1 hour?

jen: approved for 60m, we need monitoring and rollback plan. Set alarms for unscheduled pods < 50% within 20m or rollback.

kevin: patching now. running: 
```
aws autoscaling update-auto-scaling-group --auto-scaling-group-name gpu-pool-prod --max-size 18
```

kevin: update returned OK. cluster-autoscaler now sees capacity, attempting scale up. logs: 
```
I0109 09:20:05 scale_up.go:271] Scale-up: considering launch template lt-0a1b2c3d for nodegroup gpu-pool-prod
I0109 09:20:06 scale_up.go:290] Nodegroup creation initiated
```

maria: but now I see Provisioning fails for new instances: 
```
E0109 09:21:11 awsprovider.go:122] error launching instance: UnauthorizedOperation: You are not authorized to perform this operation.
```

sahil: that matches the earlier AccessDenied from assumed role. looks like autoscaler IAM role lost ec2:RunInstances or autoscaling:CreateAutoScalingGroup permission during a recent infra tweak. ops team, confirm?

support-ops: customer-impact note: multiple customers hitting timeouts; support tickets flagged with high priority. We've posted status page update (partial degraded).

alex: can we do a hotfix: manually spin up GPU instances using a service account with broader permissions then register them to the cluster? Might be faster than chasing IAM policy change.

maria: manual instance launch is possible, but they must match node labels and kubelet config and use the correct launch template (AMI + user-data). I'll try creating nodes using known-good launch template id lt-0f9e8d7c.

kevin: reminder: manual nodes must include the node taint removal step or appropriate tolerations. current GPU node taint is: node.kubernetes.io/gpu:NoSchedule. Many of our scheduling rules rely on the toleration but there's a new workload that doesn't tolerate it, causing pods to remain pending even if nodes exist.

maria: good catch. I'll create nodes with the taint removed temporarily so existing pending pods can schedule, then reapply taint after queue drains.

jen: risk: removing taint allows some CPU-only pods onto GPU nodes - could lead to noisy-neighbor issues. We'll monitor. Only do minimal number of nodes.

kevin: manual EC2 runs succeeded with temp-service role. nodes are joining the cluster (3 added). kubectl get nodes: 
```
NAME                         STATUS   ROLES    AGE   VERSION
ip-10-0-1-45.ec2.internal    Ready    <none>   1m    v1.25
ip-10-0-2-78.ec2.internal    Ready    <none>   1m    v1.25
ip-10-0-3-90.ec2.internal    Ready    <none>   30s   v1.25
```

maria: removing taint on those nodes: 
```
kubectl taint nodes ip-10-0-1-45 node.kubernetes.io/gpu:NoSchedule- 
```

maria: pods are starting to schedule. queue length dropping: 2400 -> 900 in 12m. 95th latency improving.

support-ops: updating customers: "We've provisioned temporary capacity and are routing traffic to relieve the backlog. We're monitoring and will follow up once autoscaling permissions are restored."

ops-bot: recommended next steps: 
- restore autoscaler IAM permissions (infra team)
- reconcile launch template changes (image or userdata drift)
- roll back taint removal after backlog cleared and set tolerations where needed
- add ASG safety buffer for scheduled maintenance windows

sahil: I'll open a ticket to infra: "autoscaler-role lost permissions" with logs and requested policy delta (ec2:RunInstances, autoscaling:CreateAutoScalingGroup, iam:PassRole for instance profile).

kevin: also noticed cluster-autoscaler version is 1.20.x; there was a bug that mis-evaluates taints with mixed instance types. we should plan an upgrade to latest stable. noted in ticket.

jen: maria - handing off on-call to kevin at 10:00. Are we at a stable state for handoff?

maria: handing off. Current state: temporary nodes up (3), ASG max bumped to 18, queue dropping but still above normal. Autoscaler can't create ASG due to IAM; infra ticket opened and assigned to sahil. Taint removal applied temporarily. Monitoring dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/gpu-pool. Alert thresholds: queue > 500 still firing.

kevin: taking over. I'll keep the temporary capacity until infra confirms permission fix and we see autoscaler creating nodes without manual intervention. I'll also revert taint when tolerations are updated.

sahil: infra ticket created: INC-4721. Assigned to infra-sre team. Initial triage: policy delta logged. Working with security to push emergency IAM patch. ETA 45m.

support-ops: updating status page: ETA 60m, customers informed. We'll escalate if no change.

ops-bot: post-incident actions suggested: 
- emergency runbook for autoscaler IAM regressions
- automated ASG emergency scale playbook (approve via oncall channel)
- add canary test that verifies cluster-autoscaler can create instances after infra changes
- tighten monitoring for launch template drift and taint mismatches

kevin: noted. I'll create follow-up tickets and schedule a retrospective. For now, continuing monitoring and will revert the taint once queue < 200.

maria: resolved? not fully but under control. Leaving for kevin. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated (manual capacity added). Severity: Sev2. Follow-ups: INC-4721 (IAM), RFC-310 (autoscaler upgrade), P0 playbook for ASG emergency scale.

support-ops: closing loop with customers with update.

kevin: handoff accepted. I'll post final postmortem draft after infra confirms IAM change.

end of thread.
